subject: Recap + quick curiosity check: Redwood x ClearPath discovery
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@clearpath.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + quick curiosity check: Redwood x ClearPath discovery

Hi Samantha —

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and two asks at the bottom.

Call highlights:
- Goals: reduce inference costs for nightly batch scoring and improve 99th-percentile latency for interactive analyst queries.
- Current setup: ClearPath uses an in-house batching endpoint and a mix of A100 and CPU fallback for spikes.
- Main constraints: SOC2 evidence needs, VPC deployment for sensitive datasets, and predictable monthly spend.

Potential Redwood fit (high-level):
- Hosted API for quick pilot (data controls + IP protections) or Private VPC for production handling of PII.
- Cost levers: prefix caching for repeated queries, per-route quantization recommendations we discussed.
- Typical pilot success metrics: 30–50% token cost reduction on batched workloads + sub-200ms median latency for analyst flows with dedicated pooling.

Next steps I suggested on the call:
1) I’ll send discovery notes and a 1-pager with an example pilot scope (attached).
2) If this looks directionally useful, we propose a 6-week pilot focused on the 10 most common batch jobs + one analyst route.
3) We’ll draft a simple mutual action plan (timeline, success metrics, guardrails) for procurement.

Two quick asks from you: could you (a) confirm whether procurement needs a confidentiality addendum before we share deeper logs, and (b) tell me whether this is something ClearPath wants to pilot in Q2 or if timing has slipped?

I attached the discovery notes and a concise Redwood one-pager for your internal folks. If it helps, I can propose two 15-min times next week to walk the pilot scope with your engineering lead.

Thanks again — appreciate the candid conversation.

—
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0117
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- discovery-notes-20270415.pdf (application/pdf)
- redwood-onepager.pdf (application/pdf)

Hi Samantha —

Circling back on my note below. Quick bump in case this got caught in transit — would love a thumbs-up on the two asks: procurement confidentiality addendum and whether you’re targeting a Q2 pilot.

If timing shifted, no problem — I can keep this on a light cadence and re-engage closer to your planning cycle. Alternatively, happy to block 15 minutes to walk the proposed pilot scope (I’ve got availability Wed/Thu afternoon PT).

If easier, I’ve also looped in Karthik (cc) who can help with commercial/timeline questions.

Cheers,
Camila

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Quick check on timing + offer to help with procurement artifacts

Hi Samantha / procurement team —

Wanted to check in quickly: do you need any standard documents from us to move a pilot forward (SOC2 summary, data handling checklist, sample M&A)? Tessa on our CS team can share a short packet that procurement usually finds helpful.

If the project has shifted out of Q2, no problem — a quick note on timing helps us prioritize. If you’re still considering this, I can put together a very short mutual action plan draft and a ballpark commercial that won’t bind you.

Two minute ask: could you reply with one of these options?
- Green: pilot in Q2 — procurement needs SOC2 + MSA NDA 
- Yellow: interested but Q3 timing
- Red: not a fit right now

Thanks — appreciate whatever guidance you can share.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
